name: Expo
description:
Build, ship, and monitor React Native apps with Expo and EAS, directly from Claude. Get answers from the latest Expo docs, kick off cloud builds and CI/CD workflows, submit to the App Store and Google Play, and track how your app is doing in production.

  Key features
  - Docs & setup — search and read the Expo docs, learn key topics, and add Expo libraries to your project
  - EAS builds — start, cancel, and inspect cloud builds, read build logs, and submit to the App Store
  - CI/CD workflows — create, validate, run, and monitor EAS workflows and job logs
  - Store monitoring — track App Store and Google Play reviews, crashes, and TestFlight feedback — and reply to reviews

_published_faq.name: How do I add Expo to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Expo to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Expo MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expo lists 25 MCP tools, including add_library, appstore_delete_review_response, appstore_reply_review, appstore_reviews, build_cancel, build_info, build_list, build_logs, build_run, build_submit, learn, and playstore_crashes.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Expo?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Expo in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
Expo requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Expo is developed by Expo. It is listed as partner on the Claude connector directory.
